newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIAN PRESIDENT INVITES POPE TO VISIT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIAN PRESIDENT INVITES POPE TO VISIT.

text.p: President Petar Stoyanov has invited Pope John Paul to make a first visit to predominantly Orthodox Bulgaria, the presidency said on Wednesday.

"I think that your visit to Bulgaria would be a firm gesture of support to my country and people at the present difficult time," Stoyanov, who met the Polish Pope on a visit to Rome last year, said in his invitation.
The Orthodox Church split from the Roman Catholic church over theological differences in the Great Schism of 1054.

The Bulgarian Orthodox Church is also split between followers of Patriarch Maxim and a rival faction who say he was appointed rather than elected under communist rule, and who enthroned their own patriarch, Pimen, last year.
Stoyanov was the first head of state since King Boris III to have a religious ceremony when he took office in January. He chose Pimen to conduct the blessing ceremony.
Ill-health has slowed the 76-year-old Pope's pace in recent years but he has six foreign trips planned for 1997 -- to Sarajevo, Prague, Beirut, Poland, France and Brazil.
